title: Lies Make You Hop
logline: In Pip and Dot's house every lie makes you hop, and Dot has been hopping all week to hide Pip's present.

story.premise: Rule-world sibling skit: in Pip and Dot's house, every lie makes you hop.
story.conflict: Dot keeps lying (and hopping) about what she is hiding on the desk.
story.stakes: Pip thinks his little sister has been lying to him all week, and in their house every lie is on show.
story.reveal: Bloxy bursts in and spoils it: it is a 'Best Brother' present for Pip.
story.ending: Dot says she does not think he is the best brother and hops; Pip says he is not crying and hops; Dot: "Liar."

payoff.text: Dot was hiding a Best Brother present, and the hop rule exposes how both siblings feel.

setting.description: Pip's lamp-lit bedroom at night; Dot stands guard in front of the desk with a wrapped present on it.

beats.description: Rule: in this house lies make you hop. Dot hops.
Pip asks what Dot is hiding: "Nothing." Hop.
Lie ladder: "A wall" (true, no hop), "Air" (double hop), "cardio" (hop).
Stakes land: Pip is hurt that his sister lied all week.
Bloxy bursts in and spoils the Best Brother present.
Pip, touched: "Best... brother?"
Dot: "No." She hops. Pip is not crying: he hops.
Dot: "Liar."

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: In our house, lies make you hop.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: My little sister lied all week.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Dot. What are you hiding back there?

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: You've lied all week. I thought we were a team.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: Dot! Did he find the Best Brother present?

title: He Charged a Coin to Sit in the Shade… 💀
logline: On a scorching day Rook charges a coin per sit under the town's only shady tree, until Ms. Tally reads the old sign at its trunk.

story.premise: On a scorching day Rook turns the single shady tree in town into a VIP zone and charges everyone a coin to sit under it.
story.conflict: Bloxy and Dot are stuck in the sun while Rook keeps raising the price.
story.stakes: It is the only shade in town and Rook will not share it.
story.reveal: The old sign says shade is free and whoever sells it has to water it, every leaf.
story.ending: Rook waters the tree with a tiny cup; Dot invites him to sit, teases him with his own price, then lets him in for free.

hook.text: He made the shade VIP only.
hook.question: Will anyone get to sit in the shade?

payoff.text: Rook's own rule backfires and Dot shares the shade with him for free.

setting.description: A hot, bright town square with one big round tree; an old sign stands at its trunk and a tiny cup sits on the paving.

beats.description: Rook guards the only shady tree in town like a bouncer.
Dot asks what VIP means; Rook explains.
Dot offers a coin; Rook doubles the price.
Ms. Tally walks in and points Rook at the old sign by the trunk.
Insert: the old sign. Ms. Tally reads it.
Time skip: Rook crouches with the tiny cup, watering leaf by leaf.
Dot, cool in the shade, offers Rook a seat.
Dot: kidding. The shade is free, even for Rook.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: This tree is VIP now. One coin per sit.

lines.speaker: tally
lines.text: Free shade. Sell it, you water it.

title: Put on Trial Over ONE Block
logline: Pip puts Bloxy on trial because his trophy moved one block; judge Dot zooms into the evidence and finds the real culprit.

story.premise: Pip holds 'family court' in his bedroom because his trophy moved one block to the left, and Bloxy is the accused.
story.conflict: The evidence (a time-stamped photo) points at Bloxy, and the judge takes cookie fees.
story.stakes: If Bloxy is found guilty he is banned from Pip's room forever.
story.reveal: Zoomed in, the mirror in the photo shows Pip moving the trophy for a selfie.
story.ending: Pip is sentenced to let Bloxy pick snacks for a month, apologises, and Bloxy nudges the trophy one block again: "OBJECTION!"

hook.text: Put on trial over ONE block.
hook.question: Who really moved the trophy?

payoff.text: The accuser moved his own trophy: Dot finds Pip in the photo's mirror.

setting.description: Pip's bedroom turned courtroom: the desk is Dot's bench, with Pip's trophy and his phone on top.

beats.description: Pip points at Bloxy: a trial over one block. Insert: the trophy.
Stakes: guilty means banned from Pip's room forever.
Pip shows where the trophy was; Bloxy protests it is one block.
The judge walks in: Dot, Pip's little sister, at the desk bench. She charges a cookie.
Exhibit A: Pip's daily trophy photo and the time stamps.
Even the judge goes "ooh". Bloxy's alibi backfires: he was eating Pip's cookies.
Dot orders a zoom on the mirror in the photo.
Reveal: Pip himself, taking a selfie with the trophy. Freeze on his frozen face.
Pip: "a different Pip". Dot slams the bench: guilty, Bloxy picks snacks.
Pip screams, then apologises; Bloxy accepts.
Bloxy nudges the trophy one block. Pip: OBJECTION!

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: My best friend put me on trial over ONE block.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: Guilty meant banned from his room. Forever.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: My trophy was HERE. Now it's THERE!

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: Then the judge walked in. His little sister.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Court is open. Fee is one cookie.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: He photographs it every single morning.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: It moved at nine-oh-one. You came at nine!

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: I was on your bed the WHOLE time!

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: And in the mirror... was PIP.

lines.speaker: dot
lines.text: Guilty! Bloxy picks snacks. For a MONTH.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: Then Pip mumbled the hardest words of his life.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Sorry I put you on trial, buddy.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: Then I moved his trophy. One block.

title: Whoever Laughs Loses
logline: In Ms. Tally's class, whoever does not laugh gets tomorrow off: Rook the statue versus Dot the wall.

story.premise: Rule-world classroom: in Ms. Tally's class, whoever does not laugh gets tomorrow off.
story.conflict: Show-off Rook tries everything to make blunt Dot laugh.
story.stakes: A day off for whoever keeps a straight face.
story.reveal: Rook cracks at his own dance; then the deadpan referee points out she never laughed.
story.ending: Ms. Tally takes tomorrow off, so there is no school; Dot finally laughs and is called out.

hook.text: Whoever doesn't laugh gets tomorrow off.
hook.question: Who can keep a straight face?

payoff.text: The referee wins, so everyone gets the day off.

setting.description: Block classroom; Ms. Tally referees from the board while Rook and Dot face off.

beats.description: Ms. Tally states the rule: whoever does not laugh gets tomorrow off.
Bloxy brags, sees Rook's face and laughs at once: out.
Rook the statue vs Dot. Rook dances to crack her.
Dot, deadpan: is that a dance? It looks like a sneeze.
Rook freezes, then laughs at himself: out. Respect, tiny statue.
Twist: Ms. Tally never laughed either. She takes tomorrow off.
No school for anyone: Rook and Bloxy celebrate.
Dot finally laughs. Ms. Tally: Dot. Out.

lines.text: Whoever doesn't laugh gets tomorrow off.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: Oh no. He's doing the thing.

lines.text: Correct. I win. No school tomorrow.

title: He Said Nobody Could Beat Him… Then Our Teacher Ran 😳
logline: Rook bets nobody can beat his twelve-second lava run. Quiet Ms. Tally puts the timer on and runs it holding her tea.

story.premise: Rook bets nobody can beat his lava-run record; if anyone does, he has to admit they are better.
story.conflict: Bloxy and Pip both fail, and Rook gets louder with every miss.
story.stakes: Rook's record, and his pride: he has never admitted anyone was better.
story.reveal: Ms. Tally runs it in eight seconds without spilling her tea: she is a retired Lava Run champion.
story.ending: Rook admits she is better, asks for lessons, and she tells him to bring his own tea.

payoff.text: The teacher beats the record, Rook says she is better out loud, and asks to learn.

setting.description: A wide start platform with a checkpoint flag, a lava tile on the first platform and a loop course of two more platforms that leads back to the start.

beats.description: Rook brags about his lava-run record; Bloxy states the bet in one sentence.
The stakes: Rook has never admitted anything.
Bloxy jumps first and lands on the lava tile; respawns.
Ms. Tally steps forward with her tea. Rook cannot believe it.
Ms. Tally clears the course in three jumps without spilling a drop.
Rook freezes. Ms. Tally reveals she was the champion.
Rook admits it out loud, then asks for lessons.
Ms. Tally, deadpan: Monday, bring your own tea.

lines.text: Rook bet nobody beats his lava record.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Beat it, and Rook admits you're better.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: She jumped like the lava was late for class.

lines.speaker: bloxy
lines.text: Then Rook had to say it.

title: One Button, Ten Seconds
logline: Rook parks Dot's trophy across the lava and gives her ten seconds; she built a button just for him.

story.premise: Rook takes Dot's trophy to his platform across the lava and gives her ten seconds to get it back.
story.conflict: Dot is tiny, the gap is lava, and Rook is guarding the trophy.
story.reveal: Her button plays an audience cheer; Rook turns to bow and she takes the trophy back.
story.ending: Rook admits it was genius; Dot presses the button again and he bows again.

hook.question: How will tiny Dot get her trophy back?

payoff.text: Dot outsmarts Rook's vanity with an applause button and takes her trophy back.

setting.description: Two studded platforms over glowing lava; Dot's button on the near one, Rook and the trophy on a crate on the far one.

beats.description: Rook has parked Dot's trophy on his platform across the lava.
Ten seconds to take it back. Pip: that is lava. Dot: I need one button.
Dot stomps her big floor button: an audience cheers.
Rook turns to bow to his "audience" while Dot jumps the lava, grabs the trophy and jumps back.
Rook counts down, turns: the trophy is gone. Dot holds it up. Freeze on Rook.
She built an applause button for him: he is very predictable.
Rook admits it was genius.
Dot: one more time? She stomps the button again; Rook bows again.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Your trophy lives on MY side now.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Ten seconds to take it back. Go.

lines.speaker: rook
lines.text: Thank you! Rook loves you too!

title: Someone Was Secretly Fixing Our First Obby… 🥺
logline: The tiny obby Bloxy and Pip built on their first day keeps getting fixed overnight. They stake it out and catch the last person they expected.

story.premise: Someone is secretly fixing the tiny obby Bloxy and Pip built on their very first day.
story.conflict: Nobody admits to it, so Bloxy and Pip hide behind a very thin flag to catch the fixer.
story.stakes: Their first obby, and who has been caring for it in secret.
story.reveal: It is Rook: he practised alone on their obby when he was new and nobody played with him.
story.ending: They invite Rook to play; the obby now has a fourth platform, and it is gold.

hook.text: Someone secretly fixed our first obby.
hook.question: Who has been fixing the obby?

payoff.text: The secret fixer was Rook; he is invited to play and adds a gold platform.

setting.description: A wide platform with a thin checkpoint flag, and next to it a tiny obby of three small blue platforms plus one new gold one, above the clouds at sunset.

beats.description: Bloxy stares at the tiny first obby: it looks brand new.
They built it on their very first day. They were terrible at it.
Every day a new fix, and nobody ever saw who. Bloxy suspects Pip.
They hide behind the checkpoint flag to wait. It is a very thin flag.
At sunset someone lands on the tiny obby: Rook.
Rook admits why: nobody played with him when he was new.
Bloxy invites Rook to play; Rook accepts. The obby has a new fourth platform.
Rook, to camera: it is gold. Obviously.

lines.text: Someone kept secretly fixing our very first obby.

title: The Shiny Door Is ALWAYS the Trap… Right? 🤔
logline: Two doors over the lava: one is the next level, one is lava. Pip says the shiny one is always the trap. His little sister picks it anyway.

story.premise: Ms. Tally offers two doors: one leads to the next level, one leads into lava.
story.conflict: Pip insists the gold door is always the trap; his little sister Dot picks gold anyway.
story.stakes: Pick wrong and you get the lava.
story.reveal: The plain door is the lava. Dot built the level, with a trap for people who say "always".
story.ending: Level two has the same two doors; Pip asks Dot for help and she answers "Gold. Always."

payoff.text: Dot was right because she built the level; the choice loops into level two.

setting.description: A dark lava obby at night: one wide platform with two doors side by side, a plain wooden one and a shiny gold one, the lava glowing below.

beats.description: Ms. Tally presents two doors over the lava: one is the next level, one is lava.
Pip is sure the shiny gold door is the trap. Dot picks gold anyway.
Final answers. Pip asks the viewer which door they would pick.
Pip pushes the plain door: lava. Dot pushes the gold door: level two.
Dot built this level. The trap was built for Pip.
Level two: the same two doors. Pip asks his sister for help.
Dot: gold, always. Pip freezes.

title: My Loudest Fan
logline: Pip's little sister cheers so loud he flinches at the last jump; when she finally goes quiet, he learns he cannot jump without her.

story.premise: Dot is Pip's loudest fan on the sky obby, and every scream makes him flinch at the last jump.
story.conflict: Pip snaps at her to be quiet for one jump.
story.stakes: His first ever gold flag, and his sister's feelings.
story.reveal: In the silence he realises he can't jump without her cheering.
story.ending: He asks her to cheer louder, clears the jump; Dot clears it first try and makes him cheer for her: "LOUDER."

hook.text: My sister cheered. I couldn't jump.
hook.question: Will Pip ever make the jump?

payoff.text: With his sister cheering again, Pip clears the jump and wins his first gold flag.

setting.description: Two studded platforms over the clouds at sunset with one big gap; the gold flag waits on the far platform.

beats.description: Dot screams GO PIP GO; Pip windmills at the edge.
One jump to his first ever gold flag.
Every attempt, a louder cheer and a flinch. Attempt seven: he falls over on flat ground.
Pip snaps: be quiet for one jump.
Dot goes quiet. The silence is the worst sound he has heard.
He cannot jump without her. "Do the thing." "Louder."
GO PIP GO: he jumps and lands on the gold-flag platform.
Gold flag, first try (well, eighth). Dot clears it first try.
Dot: now cheer for me. Pip whispers. Dot: LOUDER.

lines.text: And it was the worst sound I'd ever heard.

title: Last One to Move Wins… She Brought NOTHING 😳
logline: Ms. Tally's trophy goes to whoever moves last. Rook brought snacks, Pip brought a nap, Bloxy brought confidence, and Dot brought nothing at all.

story.premise: A stand-still challenge for Ms. Tally's trophy: last one to move wins.
story.conflict: Everyone brought an advantage except Dot, and Rook mocks her for it.
story.stakes: The trophy, and Rook's claim that he can stand all day.
story.reveal: Every advantage backfires: Bloxy dances, Pip falls asleep, Rook eats his snack. Dot never moves.
story.ending: Rook offers Dot his pizza; she refuses because she would have to move.

payoff.text: Dot, who brought nothing, wins, and stays still even after winning.

setting.description: Ms. Tally's classroom after the bell: four contestants in a row in front of the board, Ms. Tally at the side with the trophy, a pizza box on a desk.

beats.description: Ms. Tally holds up the trophy: last one to move wins it.
Each contestant shows what they brought.
Ms. Tally says freeze. Everyone locks a pose.
Bloxy celebrates too early and is out first.
Two hours later: Pip falls asleep standing and tips over.
Five hours later: Rook stares at his snack and cracks.
Dot has not moved once. She wins.
Rook offers Dot his snack: a decent loser.
Dot, still perfectly still: she would have to move.

lines.speaker: tally
lines.text: Last to move wins this trophy.

title: Not Scary at All
logline: Pip promises his little sister a not-scary first campout; when something stomps in the trees, he finds out how brave he is, and why.

story.premise: Pip promises Dot her first campout will have zero scary stuff.
story.conflict: Something stomps closer and closer in the dark trees from the first seconds; Pip hides behind his little sister.
story.stakes: Pip's promise to his little sister, and his big-brother pride.
story.reveal: The stomper is Ms. Tally on night patrol; then Dot admits she was never scared.
story.ending: Dot pretended to be scared so Pip would be brave; Ms. Tally calls back his squeaky voice.

hook.question: What is stomping in the trees?

payoff.text: Pip stood up for his sister, the monster was only Ms. Tally, and Dot planned his bravery.

Double twist: Dot was never scared; she gave Pip a reason to be brave.

story.premise: Bloxy's best friend Pip sells Bloxy's first trophy to show-off Rook for three coins.
story.conflict: Bloxy thinks Pip betrayed them for his own race entry, and Rook will not give the trophy back.
story.stakes: The trophy is from Bloxy and Pip's very first obby, and Bloxy cannot afford the race.
story.reveal: Pip used the three coins to pay Bloxy's race entry; Rook's own coins paid for it.
story.ending: Rook poses mid-race and loses, returns the trophy, and Pip calls it the best three coins he ever spent.

hook.text: Pip sold my trophy. Three coins.
hook.question: Why would Pip sell their trophy?

payoff.text: The sale paid Bloxy's race entry; Bloxy wins and the trophy comes home.

setting.description: The paved town square at the end of the street, a sign-up board for the Town Dash, and a finish flag down the street.

beats.description: Rook shows off Bloxy's first trophy; Bloxy narrates the betrayal in one sentence.
Bloxy screams at Pip; Pip shrugs it off.
Why the trophy matters: Bloxy and Pip won it together.
Ms. Tally calls the last sign-ups for the Town Dash: three coins.
Ms. Tally puts Bloxy in a lane: someone already paid. Rook realises whose coins.
Bloxy looks at Pip; Pip looks at his shoes.
Ms. Tally starts the race; both turn down the street.
Bloxy sprints; Rook stops after two steps to pose.
Rook walks over and hands the trophy back; Pip lands the button.
Pip, to camera: best three coins he ever spent.

metadata.title: My Best Friend Sold My Trophy for 3 Coins 💔
metadata.description: Pip sold my first trophy to Rook... for exactly the price of a race I could not afford. Would you forgive him? Original animated story with blocky characters.

inspiration.note: Original story written by Claude (writerB) for Blox Studio from premise 7 of the studio direction brief. Informed only by broad format patterns (first-person storytime narration, betrayal that turns out kind, rival karma plus a decent moment); no specific video, plot, line or character was used. Judged and edited 2026-10-11 (same chat session): hook text tightened to 6 words, lines trimmed so every line fits its slot at production pace 1.5 / voices 1.3x, SFX density and shot rhythm adjusted, titles checked.
